**M6: personal Gmail over IMAP/SMTP with an app password (`--provider imap`).** Google Workspace keeps using the Gmail API provider (`gmail`). This provider is for a personal `@gmail.com` account, and it also works with any IMAP server.

### Pod side

- **No behaviour change for existing accounts.** The Microsoft 365 account works as before. The MIME code that `gmail` shares with `imap` moved into a common package; its output is unchanged.
- **No new policy keys.** `mode`, `signoff`, `[send]` and `[delete]` apply to `imap` accounts as to the others. Keep `mode = "draft"`.
- **Outbound ports**: an `imap` account connects to `imap.gmail.com:993` (TLS) on every command. It connects to `smtp.gmail.com:465` (TLS) only for `email send` in send mode. The existing NetworkPolicy already allows public egress on any port.
- **Login** (once, from your own terminal; the app password goes through stdin and never through the agent):

  ```sh
  kubectl -n hermes exec -i deploy/hermes-james -c hermes -- \
    email auth login -a gmail --provider imap --mode draft --username <addr> --password-stdin
  ```

  The password is stored 0600 in `accounts/gmail/imap-credentials.json` under the config dir, so it lives on the same volume as the M365 token cache. `auth status` does not show it. Revoke by deleting the app password in the Google account. Steps: [docs/gmail-personal-setup.md](https://github.com/james-tronai/email-cli/blob/v0.5.0/docs/gmail-personal-setup.md).
- **Default account**: the M365 account stays the default. Gmail commands, including any cron job for it, need `-a gmail`.
- **Mode is client-enforced.** An app password can read, change and send. In read mode the client changes nothing, and below send mode it never opens an SMTP connection. Login prints a warning about this. `email send` on a draft-mode account exits 4 before any network call.
- **Agent-visible difference**: on `imap`, `email draft update` saves a new version, so the draft's id changes. The agent must use the id it returns. `skills/email/SKILL.md` notes this; the Pod's own SKILL copy may want the same line.
- **Connections**: one IMAP connection per command, logged out at the end. Gmail allows 15 simultaneous connections per account.

### What `imap` does

- **On Gmail** (the server announces `X-GM-EXT-1`):
  - ids are `X-GM-MSGID` in hex, and `web_link` is `mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/<id>` (`#drafts/<id>` for drafts);
  - threads use `X-GM-THRID` and labels use `X-GM-LABELS`;
  - search passes the query to `X-GM-RAW`, so it takes Gmail search box syntax.
- **On other servers**: UIDs, threads from `References`/`In-Reply-To`, folders instead of labels, and a small search syntax.
- **Sync**: `UIDVALIDITY` + `UIDNEXT`, plus `HIGHESTMODSEQ` (CONDSTORE) to skip unchanged runs. When `UIDVALIDITY` changes, it records a new baseline and reports `initialized: true`, as an expired Gmail history id does.
- **Drafts**: `APPEND` to Drafts with `\Draft`. A reply carries `In-Reply-To`/`References` and the quoted text; a forward carries the attachments. The signoff, `block_external_forward` and `require_reply_context` rules are the shared service-layer ones. `draft delete`, and the old version on `draft update`, are deleted for good: on Gmail, moved to Trash and expunged there.
- **Send**:
  1. Read the draft's RFC 822 source from Drafts.
  2. Set a fresh `Message-ID` and the sending `Date`, and drop `Bcc` from the header. Bcc recipients stay in the SMTP envelope.
  3. Submit over SMTP with the app password.
  4. Delete the draft. Gmail files the sent copy in Sent itself; on other servers the copy is `APPEND`ed to Sent.

  Idempotency, recipient rules and the audit work as in M4. The audit's result id is the `Message-ID`.

### Not yet verified against a real mailbox

All tests run against fixtures:
- a Gmail-model IMAP server written for the tests;
- go-imap's in-memory server, for the non-Gmail path, over STARTTLS;
- go-smtp.

Still to confirm on the real account:
- the `#drafts/<id>` link;
- that Gmail threads an APPENDed reply draft with its original (`require_reply_context` depends on it);
- deleting a draft through Trash.
